defects.detail: 'potestate suâ, rejicentes et renuentes, extrema pati coegêre' (compelled those rejecting and refusing to suffer extremes) -> 'compelled others to suffer extreme penalties by their own power, rejecting and refusing them' (participles attached to the kings, not the victims)

reason: Close rendering of the Beast/ten Kings argument; only the rejicentes et renuentes clause is misconstrued.

defects.detail: '若晝夜之有經' (like day and night having their constancy) -> 'like the sun and moon having their cycles'
'子天之合也' (you are one with Heaven) -> 'The Son is the union of Heaven'

reason: Yao-Shun dialogue rendered faithfully overall; 晝夜 rendered as sun and moon, and 子 (you) misread as 'The Son'.

defects.detail: opening clause 'mysteria curiosula mentis acie penetravit' (penetrated the mysteries with a keen mind) is dropped; the translation starts 'or Heathenism, that all those things...'
'illum familiari colloquio dignata est' (deigned him [Abraham] familiar converse) -> 'deemed it worthy of familiar conversation'

reason: Druids/Mamre passage is faithful apart from the dropped opening clause and the misread object of dignata est.

defects.detail: the Old English column 'ic þæt hilt þanon ... worold-cyninga' is echoed verbatim with no new translation; only the page's own printed English facing column carries the meaning

reason: Output echoes the bilingual page verbatim. The printed English column gives the meaning, but the OE half is not translated.

defects.detail: the source is a Latin Livy epitome (Col. iii-iv: 'M. Claudio Marcello Q. Fabio Labeone cos.', 'libri Numae inventi'); the translation is a Demosthenes apparatus ('Geraestus', 'Fr. 14', 'On the Peace')

reason: Translation is of an entirely different text (Demosthenes critical notes), not this page's Livy epitome fragments.

defects.detail: the source is Hesiodic hexameters 'ιππων ωκυπ[οδ]ων ... Φοιβου Απολλω[νοc]' with notes on οχεων/ἀχέων; the translation is '1604. PINDAR, DITHYRAMBS ... HERACLES OR CERBERUS TO THE THEBANS'

reason: Translation renders a Pindar dithyramb papyrus, not this page's hexameter fragment and apparatus.

defects.detail: notes on ll. 10, 11 and 13, the oblique-stroke discussion, the Moschion/Webster/Arnott paragraph and the Kith. fr. 5 reference are all dropped; the plot points lose their '(?)' qualifiers
note 9 is conflated with note 10: 'Perhaps ekrithe polemion "it was judged to be the enemy's", "the ship went to Crete..."'
'The name Phanias is known from other sources' -> 'The name Phanias is common'; 'not very strong and partly dependent on hypothetical reconstructions' -> 'weak'
the quotation 'and this is accompanied ... supplanted it' is cut, as are the Handley attributions

reason: A heavily abridged paraphrase of the commentary: whole notes and the Moschion paragraph are missing, notes 9 and 10 are merged, and hedges are dropped.

defects.detail: the footnote apparatus '1) Athen. 15, 28. ... 13) L. c.' is omitted entirely; only the markers <note>1</note>-<note>13</note> remain
'nomine Crataeogoni Euphrosynes' (under the name Crataeogonum Euphrosynes) -> 'under the name of Crataeogonon or Euphrosyne'

reason: Body text on leukoion and Crataeogonon is rendered accurately; the footnote citation list is dropped and one compound plant name is split.
The French Gulf Stream and drift passage and its three footnotes are rendered completely and accurately; I found nothing wrong.

defects.detail: the closing editorial English rendering "'Cook's account. Thoth 4th, 24th year, 4 pounds of meat ... 1 tongue," is absent from the output

reason: The meat account (minae, trotters, tongue, paunch, kidneys, Mesore entries) matches the Greek line by line; the trailing printed English rendering is dropped.

defects.detail: '設教於恩臘初歸' (taught at En; returned early in the La month) -> 'teaching in Enla'
'徹帳矣' (you have closed your school) -> 'your house is empty of books'; '叟曰敬業姓施有舍甥' (the old man said: I, Jingye, surnamed Shi, have a nephew) -> 'My nephew's surname is Shi'
'故清約同死難' (had agreed to die together) -> 'he refused to serve the new regime and died for his principles' (Xie Jin did not die; the source records a pact)
'既而解使入視胡廣動靜' (then Xie sent someone to observe Hu Guang) -> 'the Emperor sent someone'
garbled '服孝孺諸市是修死之長問泣不已孫盡死' -> fluent 'He wore the clothes of the Fang Xiaoru faction in the marketplace... His entire family was killed'
final span '賦東吳王于然而皆食其言國憲家獻春秋時汗楚人謂相調笑曰緣頭巾貧妻女求食者謂之娼夫以別貴賤' (the green-headscarf passage) is not translated

reason: The narrative opening is mistranslated in several places, the commentary invents Xie Jin's death and swaps the subject to 'the Emperor', and the closing green-headscarf passage is missing. My reading of the Chinese is only moderate.

defects.detail: 'Centeno sub Teste' (under a hundredfold witness) -> 'Under your witness'

reason: The verse catalogue of battles (Kineton, Naseby, Cornwall, Basing, Newbury, York, Marston) is faithful; 'Centeno' is lost. The place-name notes are interpretive, not invention.

defects.detail: 'vt ipsius Coni potius quàm ollam Oui effigiem' (the shape of a cone rather than an egg) -> 'the shape of a horn rather than an egg pot'

reason: A long botanical commentary (Tzacapatlis through Tacuache) rendered accurately chapter by chapter; one minor slip on the Coni/Oui comparison.
The English commentary is kept, and its Greek citations (Hesychius, Porphyry, Callimachus scholion, Mnaseas) are rendered correctly; nothing is missing.
The Dutch lines 13-29 are rendered correctly next to the retained parallel Latin (Vestibulum/Janua/Atrium); the first margin speaker list was dropped, which is a layout matter only.
